run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: Scoped to the last 3 hours (2026-11-23T14:43:48Z–17:43:48Z) of the app-265-prod-logs index, the only log index present, the evidence shows an error chain confined to one of the three clusters represented in that index, production-us-east-1 (3 of 7 documents; the other 4 are INFO 'Healthy' lines from production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1). In production-us-east-1: checkout-service logged an ERROR at 15:43:41Z that POST /api/checkout failed with 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; payment-service logged an ERROR at 16:43:41Z that 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'; and checkout-service logged an ERROR at 17:13:41Z that its 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'. Both us-east-1 error messages name the same upstream, the payment provider stripe-us, as the dependency that timed out, so the deepest cause the log evidence reaches is stripe-us failing/timing out for production-us-east-1's payment-service, with checkout-service affected as its caller. I could not check the dependency further: there is no telemetry for the external provider, Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query, and my Kubernetes access reads only production-eu-west-2, not production-us-east-1. In the cluster I can read (production-us-east-2 — i.e. production-eu-west-2), all 22 otel-demo pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, all 21 deployments report 1 ready replica, and the eu-west-2 flagd fault-injection flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adFailure and others) are all at defaultVariant 'off'; that is evidence the eu-west-2 cluster is not the failing one, not evidence about us-east-1. The log index is extremely sparse (7 documents total), so breadth across the fleet is a sample-based statement, and no latency trend should be inferred from it.

claims.text: Inside the 2026-11-23T14:43:48Z–17:43:48Z window, app-265-prod-logs matched exactly 7 documents; aggregation by cluster gives production-us-east-1 = 3, production-ap-southeast-1 = 2, production-eu-west-2 = 2, by level INFO = 4 and ERROR = 3, by service checkout-service = 4 and payment-service = 3.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T15:43:41Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:43:41Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:13:41Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'.

The two production-us-east-1 error messages name the same upstream dependency, the payment provider stripe-us (/v1/charges), as the target that timed out at 30s, and the later checkout-service circuit-breaker message names payment-service; no other cluster, service or dependency is named in any ERROR line in the window.

The production-eu-west-2 documents in the same window are INFO health statements: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 2026-11-23T15:43:41Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 2026-11-23T17:13:41Z.

The production-ap-southeast-1 documents in the same window are INFO health statements: checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 2026-11-23T15:43:41Z and payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 2026-11-23T17:13:41Z.

app-265-prod-logs is the only index in this Elasticsearch source (pattern '*'), it is green and open, and it holds 7 documents total at query time; its mapping has keyword fields cluster, level, service and a date field timestamp (not @timestamp) plus a text message field.

In the Kubernetes cluster I can read, production-eu-west-2, namespace otel-demo: all 22 pods are phase Running with ready containers and restartCount 0 (including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm), and all 21 deployments report readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, e.g. checkout and payment on ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and :2.0.2-payment.

The ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo of production-eu-west-2 defines fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad; every one has state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable').

In production-us-east-1 the fault originates upstream of payment-service: the payment provider stripe-us is timing out payment-service's /v1/charges calls at 30s, payment-service therefore reports upstream timeouts, and checkout-service is the affected caller whose payment calls fail and whose circuit breaker to payment-service opened at a 41% failure rate.

The fault is not visible fleet-wide in this log sample: at the same timestamps (15:43:41Z and 17:13:41Z) production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 record INFO health statements for checkout-service and payment-service, and eu-west-2's payment-service names a different provider integration (Adyen-eu) as responding normally.

Fault injection through the flagd feature-flag ConfigMap is rejected as the cause for the cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2): flagd-config's paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable and the other fault flags are all at defaultVariant 'off', and that cluster's pods show 0 restarts and 1/1 ready deployments. This check covers only production-eu-west-2 and says nothing about us-east-1's own flagd configuration.

When metrics access is restored, compare production-us-east-1 against a baseline: error rate and p95/p99 for the payment and checkout operations on that cluster, tagged with the data's own cluster label, to confirm the 41% failure rate checkout-service reported and to see whether payment-service latency or error rate deviated before 15:43:41Z.

Check the stripe-us provider's own status/incident record for the us-east-1 payment integration, and review payment-service's 30s client timeout, retry/backoff and checkout-service's circuit-breaker thresholds, since the observed errors are upstream-initiated 30s timeouts on /v1/charges.

Read production-us-east-1's own flagd configuration and deployment/pod state (as was done for production-eu-west-2) to rule in or out a paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable flag or a restart mechanism in the cluster where the errors occur.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or cluster-labelled metric series could be read and no missing series may be read as zero.

Jaeger was unavailable for this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the checkout→payment→stripe-us call edge and span-level error/latency evidence could not be verified.

Kubernetes access reads only production-eu-west-2; there are no objects, events or pod logs for production-us-east-1 or production-ap-southeast-1, so the cluster where the errors occur could not be inspected at pod/workload level and no Kubernetes object there can be named.

app-265-prod-logs contains only 7 documents in the whole window (7 total in the index), a very sparse sample: onset time, duration, breadth across other services and the exact failure percentage apart from checkout-service's own '41%' text are unknown, and no latency trend can be inferred.
The external payment provider stripe-us has no telemetry in the available sources, so whether the timeout is provider-side, network-path or client-configuration caused could not be verified.

Application-log queries for payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm and checkout-6578865d87-v6flf in production-eu-west-2 matched no error lines (no_data views), and the events query returned no_data; these do not prove those workloads were error-free, so eu-west-2 application health is only supported by the INFO log records cited above.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so whether a deployment, configuration or provider change preceded the us-east-1 errors could not be checked.
next_steps: Restore or verify reachability of the Prometheus and Jaeger targets for this environment so the payment/checkout error rate and call chain can be measured rather than inferred from three log lines.

Obtain read access (or export) for production-us-east-1 and production-ap-southeast-1 Kubernetes state and events, to check payment-service/checkout-service pods, restarts and any flagd fault flags in those clusters.
Collect continuous payment-service and checkout-service logs for production-us-east-1 around 15:00–17:43Z to establish onset, duration and blast radius beyond the 7 sampled documents.
Obtain the stripe-us provider's incident/status information and payment-service's client timeout and retry settings to determine why /v1/charges calls took the full 30s.

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
